Hey, contacting a lawyer to find out what to expect is a good thing, but I hope you will give her the time she needs to think before you move forward with anything. This may seem fucked up, especially with how you're feeling right now, but it needs to happen for several reasons:

1) Do not make any rash decisions.

You need time to think too. Sleep on it for several nights. Give yourself time to process the fucked up shit that's swimming in your mind. You just got married, things seemed great only they weren't. Something fragile finally buckled between you. You need to figure out what it is. You need to find out if you truly, deeply, and completely LOVE her. Since you just got married, and you were optimistic up until the phone call, my gut tells me that you'd walk through fire for her; even now.

I've been where you are right now. I've made stupid, petty, and counterproductive decisions in the heat of the moment because I was hurting so bad that I just wanted it to have never happened in the first place. So I tried to erase it, ignoring that she had told me that she needed time to sort things out, that she hadn't made any decisions.

You know what doing that did? It proved to her that I was not ready for something so important. It showed her that, when everything was falling down around me, I would run like a little bitch crying for my mommy. It literally pushed back the date of our amicable reconnection by Years. Yes, years.

2) She has not made a final decision about anything.

Ignore the fag in the assless leather chaps that she's crushing on. Know that she chose to marry you for reasons that should be clear by now but might need to be discussed when both of you finally have your heads on straight. Women, like men, can't help but fantasize about a relative stranger -- it's human nature -- especially when things aren't good at home.

That crush is nothing but a symptom of a much larger problem that she, or both of you, have been ignoring for as long as you have gotten serious about your relationship. That's human nature too. When we first fall for someone we give them the benefit of the doubt. We give them a fuckton of it. Like all things, though, that well runs dry and then shit starts to die and to rot quickly.

3) You asked her to tell you what problems she's referring to.

This ties in to the thing above. There have always been 1 or more problems. She said as much. She's felt it in her heart for a long time, even though she hasn't admitted it to herself until now. She needs to think about everything you've said and asked of her.

She's not looking for excuses to divorce you. She fucking said YES to marrying you and then actually jumped through all of the appropriate hoops with you. Again, that's not something she did on a whim, neither is it something she's willing to let die on a whim either.

That "older married couple quarantine" you're referring to isn't "step 1 to divorce." She, and you for that matter, need that space away from eachother so that you can think rationally, without having the emotions that seeing each other will and does trigger and overwhelm you.

4) Limbo is not hell.

I know it may seem like it, because our brains love to imagine the worst when it's not given any input, but you need to take a deep breath and wait. She's in limbo too, don't think for a second that she's not.

Find something to keep you busy when you're feeling overwhelmed with emotion. Let yourself cry too. Use this time in limbo like she is, to figure out: wtf went wrong?! Can it be fixed????
